findings.evidence: title is "Cascadia Regional Transit: Route Updates" but the page heading is "Rider service updates" and the body covers station updates, schedule, and fare adjustments
findings.fix: Rename the title to match the page's actual subject, e.g. "Cascadia Regional Transit: Rider Service Updates".
findings.violation: The page title doesn't match the h1 or the actual content scope, which is misleading in browser tabs, bookmarks, and search results.

findings.evidence: "Riders should review the updated schedule at any station kiosk. Station staff can also help with the same request in person." followed immediately by "Commuters can report a service issue by calling rider services. Station staff can also help with the same request in person."
findings.fix: Write a distinct closing sentence for each paragraph, or drop the repeated sentence from one of them.
findings.violation: The identical closing sentence is reused verbatim for two unrelated tasks, reading as templated filler rather than written content.

findings.evidence: `src="/img/platform-update.jpg"` with `alt="Crews repainting the accessible parking spaces near the station entrance."`
findings.fix: Replace the alt text with an accurate description of the actual image content, or move the image to a section it's relevant to.
findings.violation: The alt text describes parking-lot repainting work, which has no connection to the surrounding content about checking schedules and reporting issues, and doesn't match what the filename ("platform-update") suggests.

findings.fix: Add a `<caption>` such as "Current zone status" inside the table.
findings.violation: The table has no `<caption>`, so screen reader users navigating by table don't get a programmatic description of what the table represents.

findings.evidence: "Riders can report a service issue by calling rider services. Updates post to the schedule page within one business day."
findings.fix: Rewrite the paragraph so both sentences pertain to the same topic, e.g. state how long it takes rider services to respond to a reported issue.
findings.violation: The second sentence (about posted updates) doesn't logically follow from the first (about reporting an issue by phone); it reads as a mismatched/templated sentence pair rather than coherent guidance.

findings.evidence: "Local residents can check real time arrivals through the online portal. A confirmation message follows once the request is processed."
findings.fix: Either remove the second sentence or rewrite the paragraph around a single coherent action.
findings.violation: Checking real-time arrivals isn't a "request" that generates a "confirmation message," so the two sentences describe unrelated processes stitched together.

findings.evidence: "Riders can check real time arrivals at any station kiosk. Updates post to the schedule page within one business day." (the second sentence is a verbatim duplicate of the one in `s3-p1`)
findings.fix: Write fare-adjustment-specific status text for this card instead of reusing the arrivals/update sentences.
findings.violation: This combines an unrelated real-time-arrivals statement with a one-business-day update sentence already used elsewhere, producing redundant and incoherent copy under the "Fare adjustments" heading.

findings.evidence: `<div class="icon-delete" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Delete item" id="s3-customcontrol">`
findings.fix: Remove this control if it's leftover/unused, or if needed, implement it as a native `<button>` with a label describing what it actually deletes.
findings.violation: A "Delete item" control has no apparent purpose on a public rider-information page about route/fare updates, and it's built as a non-native custom control (div with role="button") rather than a `<button>`, which risks missing keyboard activation behavior.

findings.fix: Remove the wizard block if it doesn't belong on this page, or if a real multi-step flow is intended, mark it up as an ordered list with the current step indicated via `aria-current="step"`.

findings.evidence: `read the accessibility improvements list` inside "For the full list of upcoming adjustments, ..."
findings.fix: Change the link text to match the destination, e.g. "read the full list of fare adjustments."
findings.violation: The link text promises an "accessibility improvements list" but points to `/fares/history`, which is misleading, especially for screen reader users who navigate by link text alone.

findings.evidence: `<label for="phone" id="s3-form-phone-label">Phone number (required)</label>` paired with `<input id="phone" type="tel">`
findings.violation: The label text states the field is required, but the input has no `required` or `aria-required="true"` attribute, so assistive technology and form validation won't actually treat it as required.

findings.fix: Remove the static `aria-invalid="true"` and only set it dynamically after validation fails.
findings.violation: `aria-invalid="true"` is hardcoded in the markup before any user input, so screen readers will announce the field as invalid on page load even though nothing has been entered yet.
